key_insight: Combining infrared-informed laser-power adjustment with simulation-guided external cooling sustained epitaxial CMSX-4 growth to nearly twice the build height achievable with process control alone.
engineering_relevance: Improved heat extraction supports taller single-crystal superalloy builds by laser-directed energy deposition, while optimized heat treatment reduces solutionizing time by 47%.
method: Dynamically adjust laser power using in-situ infrared thermal feedback.
Apply simulation-guided external cooling to stabilize solidification conditions.
Optimize heat treatment and compare aged microstructures with Bridgman-processed samples.
evidence_signal: EBSD validated continuous single-crystal growth, near-constant primary dendrite arm spacing indicated steady solidification, and aged precipitate distributions were similar to those in Bridgman-processed samples.
watch_item: The abstract demonstrates long cylindrical rods but does not establish transferability to complex geometries or equivalent mechanical performance.
paper_title: Bulk CMSX-4 Single-Crystal Builds via Laser-Directed Energy Deposition: Epitaxial Stability and Microstructure Evolution
